chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Do not anoint yourself with oil containing musk or ambergris when you intend to enter the state of Ihram, because its scent will remain in your head after you have entered Ihram. And anoint yourself with whatever oil you wish when you intend to enter Ihram. Once you have entered Ihram, the oil becomes forbidden for you until you exit the state of Ihram.

key_terms.إحرام: State of consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.تحل: To exit the state of Ihram

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on using scented oil before and during Ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani’s chain clarifies the juristic distinction between the permissibility of applying scented oils prior to entering the state of Ihram and their prohibition once the ritual boundaries are established. It specifically notes that while one may use any oil before Ihram, scents like musk and ambergris are discouraged due to their lingering fragrance, which persists after the state of Ihram begins, thereby affecting the purity of the ritual. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on removing sensory distractions and maintaining ritual cleanliness during the sacred state.
